look_here_first: Crush-free visual ID starts with the tiny narrow leaves: damianita is a low woody-based subshrub with many very narrow aromatic gland-dotted leaves and solitary bright-yellow heads held above the canopy on slender peduncles.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: evergreen aromatic subshrub with woody lower stems

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: many short linear to linear-oblanceolate leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves conspicuously oil-gland dotted under magnification

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: solitary terminal radiate heads on slender peduncles

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: bright yellow ray florets surrounding yellow disc florets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: involucre with relatively few phyllaries and conspicuous oil glands

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: inferior ovary maturing into a cypsela

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: Good Asteraceae whole-plant-to-head lesson: aromatic/gland-dotted narrow foliage gets you close, then involucre, ray/disc florets and cypsela/pappus confirm the composite structure.

key_traits.text: Joey shows the whole plant and flower heads in thin limestone habitat and mentions aromatic foliage and Tageteae.
